To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the level of acid-solubles in the blood of asthma patients increases and that it correlates with severity of clinical symptoms and lipid peroxidation.
the concentration of AMM in blood of bronchitis patients is higher than in the healthy subjects.
the level of acid-soluble metabolites in the blood of asthma patients is increased and is in correlation with the level of lipid peroxidatation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the level of AMM in BA and CAB patients, the correlation of their content with LPO, and the effect of hemosorption on the level of AMMs and LPO.
the concentration of AMM and LFO in the blood of 40 patients with BA, and the influence of hemosorption on their concentration.
the role of AMM and LOP in the pathogenesis of BA and CAB.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AMM content in the blood of asthmatics is an important indicator of the severity of the disease and the effectiveness of therapy.
the level of the acid-soluble middle mass metabolites (AMM) in the blood of asthmatic patients increases in proportion to the severity of their disease.
AMM are the products of the metabolism of proteins, lipids and carbohydrates in the body of patients with BA and CAB.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the increase in the concentration of AMM and LPM in blood is a result of the increased activity of LPO and is a marker of severity of BA and CAB.
the increase in the level of AMM in patients with BA and CAB is a consequence of the increase in LPO products.
the AMM are the most sensitive and informative indicator of the severity of the disease and the effectiveness of the treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the blood of bronchoasthmatics contains a number of toxic products, including the AMM.
the level of the derivatives from protein and lipid metabolism, including AMM, is increased in the blood of CAB patients and is correlated with LPO.

the level of AMM in blood is an indicator of the severity of the clinical picture of BA and CAB, and the removal of toxic products of the body by means of hemosorption leads to the normalization of the blood composition and to clinical remission.
